title: Host tests: rf_health CMake -std flag surgery fails confusingly if COMPILE_OPTIONS unset
description: lichen/tests/rf_health/CMakeLists.txt:24-27 uses get_target_property + REMOVE_ITEM to swap -std=c23 for -std=c2x (gcc-13 on the Linux builder). If lichen_test_target is ever bypassed/reordered, get_target_property returns RF_HEALTH_OPTS-NOTFOUND which lands on the compiler command line as a filename. Robust fix: check_c_compiler_flag probe in lichen/tests/cmake/test_common.cmake (benefits all host tests) or list(FILTER ... EXCLUDE REGEX '^-std='). Found in edge-cases review of bead 0hvq (worker1).
close_reason: Fixed by deleting the surgery outright (commit e4f2bc9c32): test_common.cmake's lichen_test_target has probed the compiler via check_c_compiler_flag and selected -std=c23/-std=c2x since 19fe1263ae (2026-08-30), so the per-target get_target_property/REMOVE_ITEM/APPEND block in rf_health/CMakeLists.txt was redundant — removing it eliminates the RF_HEALTH_OPTS-NOTFOUND failure mode entirely rather than hardening it (the probe was the bead's preferred root fix and already existed). Verified: clean rebuild of lichen/tests/rf_health under gcc-13.3.0 (probe picks -std=c2x), ctest 1/1 pass. 3x codereview (kimi-k3): PASS/PASS/PASS. Pass-3 observation filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-m2r9 (stale rpl_root_sig NOTE, P4).
